Class IuEntityDao<K, I, T extends Consumer<I>>

java.lang.Object
edu.iu.dao.IuEntityDao<K,I,T>
Type Parameters:
K - key type
I - contract interface type
T - entity type
public abstract class IuEntityDao<K, I, T extends Consumer<I>> extends Object
Keyed CRUD over one entity type, on top of an IuDao.

The verbs line up with a keyed collection: load(Object) reads one row, search(Map, int, Integer) lists a range, save(Object, Object) writes one row whole, and delete(Object) removes one. A subclass names the key type K, the contract interface I its callers read and write, and the entity type T that stores it; the entity implements the contract and takes a contract value's own columns through Consumer.accept(Object).

This is not an ORM, any more than IuDao is: there is no persistence context, dirty checking, or lazy loading. Each verb is an explicit read or write through the IuDao, and a save is an explicit merge: the row already stored under the key is read, the input applied onto it, and the result written back. Call the verbs inside a JTA transaction: a save reads before it writes, and related rows are written by separate statements.

Default behavior suits an entity class with a single @Id property. A DAO with a composite key overrides id(Object), key(Object) for its entity, and validate(Object). EffectiveDated entities and interface or record entities are not supported: a save would supersede rather than update, and an entity that cannot be populated cannot take its input.

Hooks

Related rows are handled by overriding afterLoad(K, T), beforeSave(K, T, I), afterSave(K, T, I) and beforeDelete(K, T); beforeSave(K, T, I) is also where a subclass stamps audit columns. None of these shares a name with a public verb: when one did, a call such as childDao.delete(childEntity) resolved to the more specific hook rather than the verb, and ran the hook without deleting the row.

Writes

A save applies its input onto the row already stored under that key when there is one, so columns the input does not carry -- when the row was created, which parent it belongs to -- survive an update. A row belonging to a parent is written through save(Object, Object, Consumer), whose binding step names the parent on a new row and is expected to refuse moving an existing one to a different parent.

Listing

search(Map, int, Integer) reads every matching row, orders them by order(), and populates related rows for the requested range only. That suits tables of registrations, not tables that grow without bound.

Access from sibling DAOs

The key methods are protected, so a DAO in another package than this class may not call them on a sibling DAO. A family of DAOs that do so, such as a parent generating keys for a child's rows, redeclares them in a common base class in its own package.

    • key

      protected K key(I input)
      Reads the key from input, when the input carries one.

      Most contract interfaces do not name their own key, so by default a key is only reachable from input that is itself a key, or an entity read back from this DAO. A DAO whose contract names the key overrides this.

      Parameters:
      input - input
      Returns:
      key; null if the input does not carry one

    • afterSave

      protected void afterSave(K key, T entity, I input)
      Performs secondary writes after the row itself is saved.

      Related values are read from the input rather than from the entity: an entity only takes its own columns from the input, so a child collection the input carries is not on the entity.

      Parameters:
      key - key the entity was saved under
      entity - entity as saved
      input - input the entity was saved from

    • searchWhere

      protected Iterable<T> searchWhere(String where, Object... args)
      Searches for entities by SQL criteria.

      Not public, and not named search: the clause is emitted into SQL verbatim, and a search(String, ...) overload beside a subclass's search(String parentId, ...) made a call passing null ambiguous. Qualify the entity's own columns with its table alias; see IuSqlBuilder.getTableAlias(Class, String). Unlike search(Map), this is not served from the transaction's read cache.

      Parameters:
      where - where clause, with ? placeholders
      args - placeholder values, in order
      Returns:
      results, in order()

    • replace

      protected static <C,R> void replace(Iterable<? extends C> desired, Iterable<R> current, Function<C,R> save, Consumer<R> remove)
      Replaces a set of related rows with those an input names.

      A null desired leaves the related rows alone, which is what an input that does not carry them means. An empty one removes them all.

      Type Parameters:
      C - related input type
      R - related key type
      Parameters:
      desired - related input the rows should now match; may be null
      current - keys of the related rows as they stand
      save - saves one related input, answering the key it was saved under
      remove - removes the related row with a key no longer named
